title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents read images embedded in Word, PowerPoint and PDF files
summary: The briefing's feature description, roadmap details, licensing statements and documented controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes image understanding from text-only embedded knowledge and leaves the feature-specific default, switch and pricing unresolved.

claims.claim: For SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge, Copilot searches files, folders or sites the user can access.
claims.quote: When you configure your agent to use SharePoint and OneDrive content as knowledge, Copilot searches SharePoint and OneDrive files, folders, or sites that a user has access to for grounding information.

claims.claim: Embedded file content consists of files uploaded for knowledge when building an agent in Agent Builder.
claims.quote: If you're using Agent Builder to build your agent, you can upload files directly from your device or the cloud to embed the content for your agent to use as knowledge.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Information Barriers is not supported on embedded files.

claims.claim: Any user with access to the agent can see responses grounded in its embedded file content.

claims.claim: The agent-details page says embedded knowledge agents use only uploaded-file text for grounding.
claims.quote: Embedded knowledge agents support uploading files as knowledge sources. Copilot only uses the text content of these files for grounding.

claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Risk assessment; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The block action prevents users across the organisation from using the selected agent, rather than disabling image reading alone.
claims.quote: Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and their other Microsoft 365 host products.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking agents created with SharePoint or Foundry affects only their Copilot Chat availability.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is enabled through SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
### Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Risk assessment; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits site-content discovery in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security and identity
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences using content already in use, such as summarising an open document.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to have a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery also requires SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites.
claims.quote: Review the SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites, including: SharePoint Online PowerShell module requirements; Role-based access control (RBAC) role assignments

claims.claim: User access is configured through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.

claims.claim: User access provides All users, No users and Specific users or groups choices.

claims.claim: User access controls who can access and install agents and plugins, not the content an agent reads.
